chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Salama b. al-Khattab from Ibrahim b. Muhammad from Imran al-Za'farani from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him).

He said: There is no man who supplicates and then seals his supplication by saying 'Whatever Allah wills — there is no power except by Allah' (ma sha'Allah, la quwwata illa billah) except that he is answered.

key_terms.لا قوة إلا بالله: There is no power except by Allah — acknowledging sole divine sovereignty
key_terms.ما شاء الله: Whatever Allah wills — an expression of submission to divine will

ai.seo_question: What phrase should you say at the end of your du'a to ensure it is answered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) teaches that sealing one's supplication with the phrase 'ma sha'Allah, la quwwata illa billah' (whatever Allah wills — there is no power except by Allah) guarantees that the prayer will be answered. This phrase acknowledges complete dependence on God's will and power, combining tawakkul (reliance on God) with the act of du'a.
